proof_boundary: The monomial heat evolution, Hermite rescaling, adaptive jet and heat derivative, finite O(1/t) condition number for each fixed multiplicity, cofinal relative transport, and fixed-x uniform-floor implication are exact. No Xi adaptive relative estimate or entry-strip theorem is proved. This does not prove an all-j successor, Lambda<=0, RH, PF-infinity, or the Clay prize.

rows.claim: A positive first-jet floor uniform as t decreases to zero at fixed x persists at t=0 and therefore excludes a multiple endpoint zero.
rows.formula: If V(t,x)->V(0,x) and ||V(t,x)||>=b(x)>0 for every 0<t<=t_0, then ||V(0,x)||>=b(x)

rows.claim: The backward-heat evolution of an m-fold local zero is a finite polynomial with an exact coefficient formula.
The local heat polynomial is exactly a probabilists' Hermite polynomial on the parabolic scale.
For every t>0 the m-fold endpoint zero splits into m simple real zeros, and P_m and its first derivative have no common zero.
The time-dependent positive scaling balances both local jet components at the same parabolic order.
At fixed y, the adaptive jet derivative has an exact Hermite representation two parabolic orders lower.
For each fixed multiplicity, the adaptive heat-jet condition number is O(1/t), with a finite explicit one-variable Hermite supremum.
The multiplicity-compatible relative transport cost on one cofinal successor tends to zero and preserves every positive-time jet even if its endpoint clearance vanishes.
For any heat solution H_t=-H_xx, the adaptive jet has an exact transport derivative and is related to the ordinary first jet by an orientation-preserving map.
rows.formula: W=(H,sH_x), s=sqrt(2t); partial_t W=(-H_xx,H_x/s-s*H_xxx); diag(1,s) is in GL+(2,R) for t>0
